title: My friend said I couldn't make a game in a month. I did it. I'm still an idiot.
author: PhilosopherNearby674
selftext:
My friend roasted me, saying I had zero skills and could never make a co-op horror game like R.E.P.O.

So I spent an entire month busting my ass to prove him wrong. I barely slept some nights, learned as I went, and used AI to help me build the game.

It's called FEEDSTOCK.   
You and up to 3 friends break into houses and loot them room by room. But instead of putting your loot in a backpack, you feed it to Tally, a creature that grows bigger and more unstable the more she eats.  
Feed her too little, and your crew is in danger. Feed her too much, and she won't even fit through the door.

**How AI helped:**

* **Code:** AI wrote a lot of the game logic, and honestly, it did a pretty good job.
* **Textures:** Made with AI.
* **Advice:** AI helped me figure out pretty much everything I had no clue about.

**Where AI failed:**

* **3D models:** A mess. I had to fix or make a lot of them myself.
* **Game design:** AI could help with the code, but coming up with the core mechanics was on me.
* **Bugs:** It broke things constantly. Some bugs were so stupid that I just left them in.

So yeah, I won the bet. I went from knowing basically nothing about game development to making a playable co-op horror game in a month.

Do I know what I'm doing now? Not really.   
Is the game good enough to deserve your attention? Probably not.   
But I spent a month of my life on this thing, so at least give the video five seconds :D

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5154830/FEEDSTOCK/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5154830/FEEDSTOCK/)
